citation: Heorhiadi, V., Rajagopalan, S., Jamjoom, H., Reiter, M.K. and Sekar, V. (2016). Gremlin: Systematic Resilience Testing of Microservices.
verified_evidence_summary: Framework and controlled experiments for application-level fault injection; the paper reports a case study in which developers found unhandled corner-case failure scenarios and reports low overhead and suitability for operational microservice resilience testing.
limitations_or_cautions: Resilience-testing evaluation rather than a comparison of automated production recovery strategies; no direct participant workload or decision-quality measure reported.

citation: Chen, J., He, X., Lin, Q., Zhang, H., Hao, D., Gao, F., Xu, Z., Dang, Y. and Zhang, D. (2019). An Empirical Investigation of Incident Triage for Online Service Systems.
source_verification: IEEE/ACM metadata and accessible paper record
verified_evidence_summary: Empirical investigation of incident triage in online service systems; relevant to assignment, diagnosis and operational decision work.
limitations_or_cautions: Full-text extraction and exact operational measures still required before substantive synthesis.

citation: Chen, J., He, X., Lin, Q., Zhang, H., Xu, Y., Hao, D., Gao, F., Xu, Z., Dang, Y. and Zhang, D. (2019). Continuous Incident Triage for Large-Scale Online Service Systems.
verified_evidence_summary: Study of eight Microsoft online service systems reports incident reassignment percentages ranging from 5.43% to 68.26%, discussion items before correct assignment up to 11.32 on average, and evaluates DeepCT for automated continuous triage.
limitations_or_cautions: Operational incident records evidence workflow outcomes, not direct workload, trust or decision rationale; single-company context limits transferability.

citation: Brogi, A., Carrasco, J., Durán, F., Pimentel, E. and Soldani, J. (2022). Self-healing trans-cloud applications.
verified_evidence_summary: Proposes and evaluates an automated self-healing methodology and prototype using controlled experiments and monkey testing across application and cloud-service failures, including unforeseen failures.
limitations_or_cautions: Prototype and trans-cloud context differ from a controlled CD transactional service; human engineering outcomes are not studied.

citation: Chen, Y., Xie, H., Ma, M., Kang, Y., Gao, X., Shi, L., Cao, Y., Gao, X., Fan, H., Wen, M., Zeng, J., Ghosh, S., Zhang, X., Zhang, C., Lin, Q., Rajmohan, S., Zhang, D. and Xu, T. (2024). Automatic Root Cause Analysis via Large Language Models for Cloud Incidents.
verified_evidence_summary: RCACopilot evaluates automated cloud-incident RCA on one year of Microsoft incident data; the paper reports RCA accuracy up to 0.766 and describes diagnostic-information collection in operational use.
limitations_or_cautions: Accuracy and deployment evidence do not establish improved engineer decision quality or reduced workload; proprietary single-organisation data and evolving LLM implementation require careful appraisal.

citation: Assad, M., Meiklejohn, C.S., Miller, H. and Krusche, S. (2024). Can My Microservice Tolerate an Unreliable Database? Resilience Testing with Fault Injection and Visualization.
verified_evidence_summary: Extends Filibuster to inject database-client faults, including exceptions and Byzantine-style corrupted responses, during development and provides IDE visual feedback.
limitations_or_cautions: Companion/tool paper; evidence concerns test capability and resilience evaluation, not production recovery outcomes or human-participant performance.

citation: Jiang, Y., Zhang, C., He, S., Yang, Z., Ma, M., Qin, S., Kang, Y., Dang, Y., Rajmohan, S., Lin, Q. and Zhang, D. (2024). Xpert: Empowering Incident Management with Query Recommendations via Large Language Models.
source_verification: arXiv full text and ACM metadata
verified_evidence_summary: Empirical study of KQL use in cloud incident management and an automated query-recommendation framework; offline evaluation and production deployment are reported.
limitations_or_cautions: Query recommendation is decision support, not autonomous remediation; production deployment does not by itself identify causal effects on engineers.

citation: Huang, J., Liu, J., Chen, Z., Jiang, Z., Li, Y., Gu, J., Feng, C., Yang, Z., Yang, Y. and Lyu, M.R. (2024). FaultProfIT: Hierarchical Fault Profiling of Incident Tickets in Large-scale Cloud Systems.
source_verification: arXiv full text and ACM metadata
verified_evidence_summary: Automated fault-pattern profiling is evaluated on production incidents from 30+ cloud services; the public record reports analysis of more than 10,000 incidents and six months of deployment.
limitations_or_cautions: Postmortem classification and trend discovery are upstream of recovery; no direct participant or causal reliability comparison is established.

citation: Chen, Z., Liu, J., Su, Y., Zhang, H., Wen, X., Ling, X., Yang, Y. and Lyu, M.R. (2021). Graph-based Incident Aggregation for Large-Scale Online Service Systems.
source_verification: arXiv/author-hosted full text and DOI metadata
verified_evidence_summary: GRLIA uses graph representation learning over cascading failures and fine-grained monitoring data; evaluation uses real Huawei Cloud incidents and reports industrial deployment.
limitations_or_cautions: Aggregation narrows incident scope but is not automated diagnosis or recovery; proprietary operational data and no direct human measures.

citation: Yang, T., Lee, C., Shen, J., Su, Y., Feng, C., Yang, Y. and Lyu, M.R. (2024). MicroRes: Versatile Resilience Profiling in Microservices via Degradation Dissemination Indexing.
source_verification: arXiv full text, author repository and ACM metadata
verified_evidence_summary: MicroRes profiles resilience by measuring dissemination from system-performance metrics to user-aware metrics and evaluates two open-source plus one industrial microservice system.
limitations_or_cautions: Resilience profiling is an evaluation measure, not a recovery intervention; exact scenario and metric definitions require detailed charting.

citation: Yu, S., Wu, H., Niu, X. and Nie, C. (2025). A Systematic Literature Review on Fault Injection Testing of Microservice Systems.
source_verification: IEEE metadata and public replication-package record
verified_evidence_summary: Reviews fault-injection testing techniques for microservice systems and organises design decisions around fault-injection configuration, execution, oracle identification and evaluation systems.
limitations_or_cautions: Not a primary empirical study; full-text verification required before using review-level counts or conclusions.

citation: Owotogbe, J., Kumara, I., Van Den Heuvel, W.-J. and Tamburri, D.A. (2025/2026). Chaos Engineering: A Multi-Vocal Literature Review.
source_verification: arXiv full text and ACM metadata
verified_evidence_summary: Multivocal review of 88 academic and grey-literature sources published January 2019–April 2024; develops a chaos-engineering definition, capability taxonomy and open research issues.
limitations_or_cautions: Mixed academic and grey evidence; cannot be treated as a primary effect study and must be checked against the review's inclusion and coding decisions.

citation: Ponce, F., Verdecchia, R., Miranda, B. and Soldani, J. (2025). Microservices testing: A systematic literature review.
verified_evidence_summary: Systematic review of microservices testing, relevant for citation chasing and the boundary between resilience testing and broader microservice testing.
limitations_or_cautions: Not yet full-text charted in this review; do not use as a verified synthesis source until retrieved and appraised.
